history: A layered shot built to the Irish tricolour, usually poured around St Patrick’s Day.
whyItWorks: The three liqueurs happen to fall in the right density order, which is the only reason the drink exists.
steps: Pour the crème de menthe into a shot glass.
Layer by pouring each ingredient slowly over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on the one below. Irish cream next, then the orange liqueur.
techniqueNotes: Density order is menthe, cream, then Grand Marnier. Reverse it and the layers collapse.
name: Irish Flag
description: Green, white and orange in three clean layers.
